races.name: GS Group Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Misterdoc
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with clear class edge who should dictate terms from the front without pressure
runners_data.comment: The Ludlow win has worked out well and he sets the standard here by some way
runners_data.spotlight: Ran on well to win at Ludlow two months ago (soft) and three of the next four home have won since; sets the standard here by some way.

runners_data.name: Mr Maximillian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs pace to aim at but showed little in bumper debut
runners_data.comment: Never dangerous from off the pace when sixth in a Wetherby bumper (15-2)
runners_data.spotlight: Never dangerous from off the pace when sixth in a Wetherby bumper (good to soft; 15-2); one of three runners for the yard.

runners_data.name: Eustace Grenier
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with bumper promise but Sean Bowen chooses stablemate Sears Crossing
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise in all three bumpers but rejected by stable jockey
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped with promise in all three bumpers (soft/good) but Sean Bowen rides one of his stablemates.

runners_data.name: Jet Noir
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but well beaten in recent hurdles starts and lacks the class
runners_data.comment: Third in an Irish point; beaten 25l in a bumper and 31 in a maiden hurdle; passed over
runners_data.spotlight: Third in an Irish point; beaten 25l in a bumper and 31 in a maiden hurdle; passed over.

runners_data.name: Brewdog
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown style, fading tendency and 101 days off the track
runners_data.comment: 125-1 when tailed off in a heavy-ground bumper at Ayr in January
runners_data.spotlight: 125-1 when tailed off in a heavy-ground bumper at Ayr in January.

runners_data.name: Sears Crossing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner switching from Flat with Sean Bowen booking suggesting stable confidence
runners_data.comment: Useful Flat maiden in Ireland and joined this strong yard for 40,000gns
runners_data.spotlight: No wins in six on the Flat for Jessica Harrington but showed a fair level of ability at up to 1m4f and joined this yard for 40,000gns; lacks jumping experience but raw ability is respected.

runners_data.name: Jack Dempsey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who unseated in first two hurdle attempts, 163 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Couldn't recommend on hurdle form but ran his best race in a good-ground bumper
runners_data.spotlight: Unseated quite early in his first two runs over hurdles but finished a remote ninth at Ayr when 150-1; the only positive is the return to a drier surface, as the ground was good when runner-up on bumper debut.

runners_data.name: Palavar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type switching from Irish Flat racing with minimal credentials
runners_data.comment: Minor Flat form in six Irish starts for two different trainers; opposable
runners_data.spotlight: Minor Flat form in six Irish starts for two different trainers; wouldn't be the obvious solution.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with modest form who lacks the class for this level
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in an Irish point but it's been modest stuff under rules; readily opposed
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in an Irish point but it's been modest stuff under rules; readily opposed.

races.paceDynamic: Misterdoc will dictate this race from the front or close to it, with Jet Noir and Sears Crossing likely to track the early pace. C'Mon So may also go forward but lacks the class to sustain pressure. The lack of genuine early speed means Misterdoc can dictate at a comfortable tempo without being harried, allowing him to save energy for the finish. This race shape strongly favors prominent runners who can sit close to the pace, as the soft tempo will leave plenty in reserve for a telling move from the last hurdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Misterdoc Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Misterdoc gets an easy lead and isn't challenged for pace early.
scenarios.body: He can dictate at his own rhythm and kick clear from the last, with any prominent tracker needing to be very good to reel him in. His class advantage becomes decisive when he's allowed to control the race on his own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo becomes crawling with multiple prominent runners going too slow early.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last hurdle where stamina matters less and class tells. Hold-up horses get their chance but need serious ability to make up the ground in a short time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Jet Noir or C'Mon So force a genuine gallop from flagfall.
scenarios.body: Misterdoc faces a speed test that could find him out, opening the door for a closer or hold-up horse with better tactical speed. The sustained pace plays into the hands of horses that can finish strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or mistakes disrupt the rhythm and order.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a survival test where jumping accuracy matters more than class or tactics. Any horse left with a clear run and sound jumping can capitalize on others' misfortunes.

watchPoints.text: Misterdoc could get an uncontested lead and prove impossible to peg back given his class advantage
Sears Crossing represents value if his Flat form translates to hurdles with Sean Bowen's booking significant
Early pace will be crucial - if it's too slow Misterdoc becomes unbeatable, if genuine it opens up the race
Multiple Olly Murphy runners could impact tactics with Sean Bowen on Sears Crossing over Eustace Grenier
Ground conditions favor Misterdoc who won last time on soft but several others are untested on good

races.name: QuinnBet Highland National Handicap Chase (For The Julian Llewellen Palmer Memorial Trophy) (GBB)

runners_data.name: El Granjero
runners_data.note: Front-runner style with sustainable pace, 47 days off and OR 124 gives class edge despite 0-5 chase record
runners_data.comment: Latest Warwick conqueror (3m5f, good to soft) was completing a hat-trick
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner who is 0-5 over fences but three times runner-up in this discipline and latest Warwick conqueror (3m5f, good to soft) was completing a hat-trick; likely to run well off an untouched mark.

runners_data.name: Busty Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was second in this race last year, solid recent form but hard to win with at 1-21 overall
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in this 12 months ago and returns in form; in the mix off a competitive mark
runners_data.spotlight: Only 1-21 overall and clearly hard to win with, but he was runner-up in this 12 months ago and returns in form having been running well from 2m4f to 3m; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Fortunedefortunata
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with cheekpieces back on after showing promise on stable debut, needs tactical race
runners_data.comment: 100-1 third at Haydock and if as good again here he could have some say
runners_data.spotlight: Had smart form when with Gordon Elliott before losing his way and selling for £3,000; fell midrace on stable debut but, with the cheekpieces back on, he outran odds of 100-1 to finish a fairly close third at Haydock (3m4f, good); if as good again here then he could have some say.

runners_data.name: President Scottie
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner but 0-9 over fences and poor recent form makes him hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Expensive to follow over fences and fair to say that others arrive here in better form
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner; has been expensive to follow over fences (0-9) and fair to say that others arrive here in better form.

runners_data.name: Gringo d'Aubrelle
runners_data.comment: Superior hurdle form is reflected in this lower chase mark; still entitled to run well
runners_data.spotlight: Superior hurdle form is reflected in this lower chase mark; 0-8 in this discipline but was third over 3m4f at Leopardstown before pulling up in a Listed handicap at Navan; no surprise to see him run well as drying ground won't faze him.

runners_data.name: Breeze Of Wind
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with new blinkers, assured stayer but pulled up two runs ago raises concerns
runners_data.comment: Pulled up two runs back but solid efforts in defeat on either side of that; assured stayer
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up two runs ago but solid efforts in defeat on either side of that and he's an assured stayer at this trip; the blinkers are new, as were the cheekpieces when third at Kelso last month.

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Prominent style, turned corner after wind surgery and clear Sedgefield win shows renewed confidence
runners_data.comment: Raised 8lb for his Sedgefield romp but had become very well handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Not as good as he was but has turned a corner following wind surgery and came home clear at Sedgefield (3m2f, good); that race fell apart in behind but he would probably have won anyway; raised 8lb but had become very well handicapped.

runners_data.name: Express Surprise
runners_data.note: Prominent tracker in excellent form with 3 wins in last 4 starts, handles this trip well
runners_data.comment: Sound jumper who stays well and he's won three of his last four; progressive
runners_data.spotlight: Only defeat in his last four races came in a good-quality 3m4f handicap at Windsor; jumped well and stayed on best at Chepstow last time (2m7f, soft) where the front two pulled well clear; raised 7lb but Ned Fox takes away 3lb out of that; respected.

runners_data.name: Brandt
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose form has declined this season, 0-18 trainer record over 14 days concerning
runners_data.comment: 3m4f chase winner last year and some sign of returning to form on his last run
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 3m4f handicap chase at Leopardstown in March of last year (yielding); this season hasn't gone so well but it wasn't too bad a run on his return to fences at Downpatrick last time (3m4f; yielding to soft) and unwise to put a line through him.

runners_data.name: Noble Birth
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 1-8 chase record and tailed off in claiming hurdle last time suggests decline
runners_data.comment: Last seen tailed off in an Irish claiming hurdle; needs a revival and has topweight
runners_data.spotlight: 3-24 over hurdles and 1-8 as a chaser; left Gavin Cromwell after finishing tailed off in a claiming hurdle in early March (tried blinkers); needs a revival and he's got a lot of weight.

runners_data.name: Fever Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won impressively at Warwick on good ground, excellent recent form profile
runners_data.comment: Hosed up at Warwick and could take some beating if the ground is bordering on good
runners_data.spotlight: If the ground is bordering on good then this 8yo could take some beating as he hosed up at Warwick last month (3m, good) on his second run after a break; the 8lb rise isn't the end of the world.

runners_data.name: Upfordebate
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won 4 times last summer, high in ratings but ran well from front at Carlisle
runners_data.comment: Four wins this season; unproven over this far and he does race up with the pace
runners_data.spotlight: Went chasing last summer and he's won four times from 3m to 3m2f; now high in the ratings but still ran very well from the front at Carlisle last month (3m); unproven over this far and he does race up with the pace.

races.paceDynamic: El Granjero will take them along at a sustainable pace from the front, with Breeze Of Wind, Stratagem, Express Surprise and Upfordebate tracking in the prominent positions behind. The lack of natural pace-forcers means this will develop into a tactical affair through the middle stages, before quickening from 2 furlongs out. With only one confirmed leader and several prominent runners content to sit and wait, the race sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses to pick off the leaders in the closing stages. This pace scenario strongly favours the patient hold-up brigade who can unleash late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady through the middle stages as expected
scenarios.body: The tactical nature allows hold-up runners to conserve energy before unleashing finishing kicks that the prominent pack cannot match. Horses like Fever Dream and Fortunedefortunata can time their moves perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners increase the tempo from 3 furlongs out
scenarios.body: The sustained pressure from the tracking pack breaks El Granjero's resolve and prevents the hold-up horses from getting into contention. Express Surprise and Stratagem can kick clear in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Lasts
scenarios.trigger: If El Granjero gets an uncontested lead and finds reserves
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to dictate throughout and hold off late challenges. His class edge over fences finally shows through in this extended trip test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is even slower than anticipated
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of position, creating an unpredictable finish. The best finishers on the day prevail in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Gringo d'Aubrelle is a non-runner which removes a potential hold-up challenger from the equation
Watch Express Surprise and Fever Dream for the strongest finishes if the pace sets up as expected
El Granjero's jumping under pressure will be crucial if challenged by the prominent trackers
Fortunedefortunata's jumping reliability remains unproven after falling on stable debut
The 3m6½f trip will test several horses at their stamina limits in the closing stages

races.name: Perth Racecourse Racing & Events Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jupiter Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from in-form Nicky Richards yard, won readily last time when well-backed and raised only 6lb
runners_data.comment: Justified market support last time; raised 6lb but appeals as a horse with more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who was very well backed at Carlisle three weeks ago and ran out a ready winner (3m1f, good to soft); raised 6lb but appeals as a horse with more to offer.

runners_data.name: Roaring Conquest
runners_data.note: Strong closer who boxed on well in deep Uttoxeter handicap, class 3 handicap winner on reappearance
runners_data.comment: Positive last run; looks sure to stay this far and has the assistance of Sean Bowen
runners_data.spotlight: A winner the last time he contested a Class 3 handicap (on reappearance) and he was boxing on when beaten a little under 10l in a deep Uttoxeter handicap last time out (2m7f, soft); looks sure to stay this far and has the assistance of Sean Bowen.

runners_data.name: Whistle Stop Tour
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning to hurdles after poor fence efforts, 10lb claimer reduces burden significantly
runners_data.comment: Gregor Walkingshaw gets a tune out of him and returning to hurdles looks a good thing
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten/pulled up over fences on his last two starts but has each-way claims on the pick of his form over hurdles this season and Gregor Walkingshaw gets a tune out of him.

runners_data.name: Gwennie May Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on career-high mark after stable switch, beaten pair at Bangor on debut for Williams
runners_data.comment: On career-high mark, off which he was no match for the front two on stable debut at Bangor
runners_data.spotlight: Won races for Dan Skelton (2m1f/2m3f) and Olly Murphy (3m1f); now on a career-high mark, off which he was no match for the front two on stable debut at Bangor (2m7f).

runners_data.name: La Zoubida
runners_data.note: Reliable closer from Nicky Richards stable, consistent record with multiple wins around this trip

runners_data.name: Go To War
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who got back on track at Windsor with positive ride, brief fence stint behind him
runners_data.comment: Poor last time and inconsistent; his pretty good record when fresh heightens interest
runners_data.spotlight: After a brief stint over fences he got back on track in beating 14 rivals over 3m at Windsor (soft) under a positive ride; however, there was a further reminder of his inconsistency when he dropped away tamely at Haydock in February; what does heighten interest is a pretty good record when fresh.

runners_data.name: Inferno Sacree
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner having 40th career start, won last two making all but raised after Plumpton success
runners_data.comment: Front-runner; hat-trick bid came up shy and others in here might be better treated
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; having his 40th career start but a first over 3m when successful at Taunton and he followed up at Plumpton (3m1f; again good to soft); subsequent defeat, again under Murray Dodd, suggests others in here might be better treated.

runners_data.name: Sleedagh
runners_data.note: Prominent type with solid placed record, consistent performer at this level for in-form Russell/Scudamore

runners_data.name: Wa Wa
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse defending course winner from 12 months ago, 11-year-old veteran returning from wind operation
runners_data.comment: Won this last year off the same mark but he ran no race last time at Warwick
runners_data.spotlight: Had lots of racing in Ireland before joining this yard last year; returned from a wind operation to win this 12 months ago off this very mark but he's an 11yo now and his last two runs, over fences and hurdles, weren't that encouraging.

runners_data.name: Musique De Fee
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning to hurdles after fence problems, cheekpieces back on suggest positive intent
runners_data.comment: Beginning to look a tricky ride and she's very risky at the minute
runners_data.spotlight: Ran no race over hurdles on final run for previous yard (tried a visor) and again looked a tricky ride back over fences on debut for this one; the return of cheekpieces may help but she's very risky at the minute.

runners_data.name: Highland Fashion
runners_data.note: Closer who won over course and distance at Newcastle, held up style suits extended trip
runners_data.comment: Had a break since bleeding last time and he's still unexposed as a stayer
runners_data.spotlight: His first run at about 3m when winning at Newcastle (good to soft) and then ran second at Warwick; latest Musselburgh run wasn't too shoddy given he was held up off the pace before staying on and he reportedly bled that day; had a break since and wouldn't be fully exposed as a stayer.

runners_data.name: Coumeenoole
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.comment: Raised 9lb for winning at Bangor (2m7f) but that was as easy as you like
runners_data.spotlight: Hadn't shown any benefit for joining Dan Skelton but he put that right when stepped back up in trip at Bangor (2m7f, good), where he won pretty much as he liked after attracting heavy support; 9lb higher this time in a better race but clearly a likely contender.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Fury
runners_data.note: Front-running type who won 3m handicaps last season making all, encouraging return at Ffos Las
runners_data.comment: Ffos Las return was encouraging given the time he'd been absent and the soft conditions
runners_data.spotlight: Last season he won 3m handicaps at Doncaster and Wetherby (both on good ground); his Ffos Las return was encouraging given the time he'd been absent and the soft conditions; in this scenario he's unexposed; considered.

races.paceDynamic: Inferno Sacree and Jukebox Fury are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead over this 3m2½f trip. Inferno Sacree has been making all in his recent wins at Taunton and Plumpton, while Jukebox Fury won his 3m handicaps last season leading from the front. With two genuine pace-setters going head-to-head early, they'll create an honest gallop that will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the extended distance. This honest pace scenario strongly favours the hold-up horses who can conserve energy early and finish with a sustained challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Inferno Sacree and Jukebox Fury engage early and maintain strong gallop
scenarios.body: The two front-runners will create genuine pace that stretches the field and sets up the race for closers. Hold-up horses like Jupiter Des Mottes and Roaring Conquest can track the pace and unleash finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner drops out leaving moderate gallop
scenarios.body: Without sustained pressure, the remaining leader gets soft fractions and kicks clear late. Prominent racers who can track and challenge get ideal scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Muddling Affair
scenarios.trigger: If both pace-setters go too fast and burn out early
scenarios.body: The early pace-setters tie up badly leaving a scramble among the pack. Mid-division horses who avoid the early burn-out can pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Inferno Sacree gets uncontested lead with soft fractions
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace pressure, the leader can dictate terms and prove hard to catch. The front-runner gets dream scenario with controlled pace.

watchPoints.text: Inferno Sacree and Jukebox Fury must be monitored for early pace battle that could compromise both
Jupiter Des Mottes was heavily backed last time suggesting stable confidence and may repeat market moves
Whistle Stop Tour switches back to hurdles after fence struggles with 10lb claim providing significant assistance
Go To War needs positive ride like at Windsor to be effective and any hold-up tactics would be concerning
Highland Fashion returns from 82-day break which could either freshen him up or leave him needing the run

races.name: Join Racing TV Now Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: He Knows Better
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form but faces traffic dangers in a congested race where four horses want similar positions
runners_data.comment: Ran well to be third in a Class 3 at Newbury that didn't go entirely like clockwork
runners_data.spotlight: Went up 5lb for beating an exposed rival at Southwell (2m4f, soft; fine on good to soft) but he still ran well in a Class 3 at Newbury (2m6f) that didn't go entirely like clockwork; he could yet raise his bar higher; much respected.

runners_data.name: Dixie Mafia
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 92 days off the track and maiden over hurdles makes him vulnerable despite point-to-point success
runners_data.comment: Respectable runs in handicap hurdles; dual point winner who could do better over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden over hurdles but ran respectably in his handicaps and this dual point winner could well do better over fences; has been off since January but one to consider, especially if at all strong in the betting.

runners_data.name: Solly Attwell
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse ideally positioned to benefit from expected strong pace and avoid the prominent traffic, back on preferred good ground
runners_data.comment: Out of form and much depends whether this return to better ground can inspire
runners_data.spotlight: Back-to-back wins over similar trips to this last September and on good or yielding ground that he's not had in his last four races; however, current wellbeing is an issue and so too the blinkers in which he was tailed off last time when first fitted.

runners_data.name: Bo Cruz
runners_data.comment: Probably better again in defeat last time but a 2lb rise is mean given he was beaten 10l
runners_data.spotlight: Much better chaser than hurdler, winning Class 5s at Catterick (3m1f) and Wetherby (3m; again on soft); wouldn't have beaten the winner in a Class 3 at Bangor even had he not clouted the last fence but that was still a fine run; 2lb rise is a bit mean given he was beaten 10l.

runners_data.name: Rock On Jet
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader but 3m trip is unproven and may not have the stamina reserves for sustained front-running
runners_data.comment: Won over hurdles off a similar mark but his chase form lacks a bit of substance
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a 3m Irish point but has never raced beyond about 2m over jumps; won over hurdles off a similar mark but his chase form lacks a bit of substance.

runners_data.name: Mumford's Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Dan Skelton's strong strike-rate and tactical advantage of avoiding early pace battles
runners_data.comment: As good as ever two runs ago; now in cheekpieces; drying ground would be a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten over a marathon trip last time but looked as good as ever when winning at Doncaster (3m, soft) two starts ago; must have a chance in first-time cheekpieces, though may not be favoured by the drying ground.

runners_data.name: Celestial Fashion
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has been raised 16lb by handicapper after back-to-back wins, making her task much tougher
runners_data.comment: Last to finish at Carlisle and it could be that the handicapper has caught up with her
runners_data.spotlight: Shot up 16lb for her back-to-back wins (2m3f/2m5f) and, although a bad mistake was no help when last to finish at Carlisle, it could be that the handicapper has caught up with her.

runners_data.name: All Inn Hand
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 321 days absence which creates significant fitness concerns despite previous course form
runners_data.comment: Winning chase debut last June; long absence is perhaps a greater concern than the 4lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Won an uncompetitive novice hurdle (2m6f, good) last May and the following month made a successful chase debut at Hexham (3m, good to soft); a long absence is perhaps a greater concern than the 4lb rise.

races.paceDynamic: Rock On Jet and Celestial Fashion will ensure a proper gallop from the start, with Rock On Jet particularly keen to lead having shown front-running tendencies. Four horses (He Knows Better, Dixie Mafia, Bo Cruz, All Inn Hand) all want prominent positions behind the leaders, creating congestion and potential interference from the third-last fence. The honest pace should set up perfectly for the two hold-up horses Solly Attwell and Mumford's Magic to time late runs. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the traffic and benefit from the solid gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest and the prominent pack gets bunched up approaching the business end
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will find out the leaders while traffic problems compromise the prominent runners. Solly Attwell and Mumford's Magic can pick their way through late with clean runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners avoids the traffic and gets first run on the leaders
scenarios.body: He Knows Better or All Inn Hand could time their move perfectly from an ideal stalking position. The pace will still be strong enough to set up their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Rock On Jet or Celestial Fashion find the pace more manageable than expected
scenarios.body: Despite the 3m trip being a question for Rock On Jet, a more sedate early pace could play into the leaders' hands. Celestial Fashion's class could tell if not asked to do too much early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders tire dramatically and the prominent pack comes to a standstill
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start affair would suit a horse getting a perfect trip from an unfancied position. The race could fall apart tactically with tired leaders and bunched followers.

watchPoints.text: Rock On Jet and Celestial Fashion could set unsustainable fractions early if they engage in a speed duel
He Knows Better, Dixie Mafia, Bo Cruz and All Inn Hand will create a wall of horses behind the leaders threatening interference
All Inn Hand faces serious fitness questions after 321 days off while Dixie Mafia has been absent 92 days
Solly Attwell is back on good ground for the first time in four runs after struggling on softer surfaces
Mumford's Magic drops back from a marathon trip where stamina was tested to a more suitable distance

races.name: Follow @racingtv On Instagram Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Nells Son
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from wind surgery with 41 days off, needs to prove hurdles form translates from chasing background
runners_data.comment: Below par back hurdling latest but had wind op since and stable enjoying a cracking spring
runners_data.spotlight: Better known as a chaser nowadays, but won twice over hurdles over four years ago; no real promise back hurdling six weeks ago but had wind surgery since and his stable is enjoying a cracking spring.

runners_data.name: The Dog Thief
runners_data.note: Natural leader who will ensure strong pace, promising hurdles debut suggests ability but lacks experience at this level
runners_data.comment: Second to Grade 2 winner before seeing off next-time-out winners at Market R; promising
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 3m maiden point at Alnwick in December and promising start over hurdles, chasing home a subsequent Grade 2 winner from the Willie Mullins yard at Carlisle before seeing off two next-time-out winners when landing a maiden at Market Rasen (2m4f, good to soft); a very interesting handicap newcomer.

runners_data.name: Skyjack Hijack
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from pulled-up effort, six-race winning streak in 2024 suggests class when right
runners_data.comment: Won six on the spin in 2024 but pulled up on belated reappearance in February
runners_data.spotlight: On a roll in the second half of 2024, rattling off six straight wins (2m5f-3m1f), but pulled up on belated return at Kelso at the end of February; entitled to strip fitter but can still only watch.

runners_data.name: Bold Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent third at Newcastle was more encouraging, well handicapped if returning to last season's form
runners_data.comment: Not at best this term but not disgraced latest and well treated if staging revival
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last season; hasn't scaled the same heights this time round, although latest third of six at Newcastle was a bit more encouraging and he's well handicapped if staging a full-scale revival.

runners_data.name: Jack Hyde
runners_data.note: Prominent runner back on track after Imperial Cup flop, recent Ludlow win shows he's in good heart
runners_data.comment: Fourth hurdle win when shading close finish at Ludlow latest; should go well again
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't feature in the Imperial Cup (Go Dante two places ahead of him) but back on track with his sights lowered when shading a tight finish in 2m Ludlow handicap (good) 25 days ago, taking his hurdles record to 4-12; has won over this trip; should remain very competitive off 6lb higher.

runners_data.name: Serious Operator
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was tailed off in competitive Morebattle Hurdle but had been in good form over this trip
runners_data.comment: Well held in Morebattle over 2m but in good form over 2m4f prior to that; should be in mix
runners_data.spotlight: 9yo who was tailed off at Kelso in February last time but that was the competitive Morebattle Hurdle over 2m; in good form over 2m4f prior to that, winning at Newcastle then second at Aintree (both good to soft); likely to be in the mix back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Flying Fortune
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up horse with excellent record on good going, just two days since last run suggests trainer confidence

runners_data.name: Letterston Lily
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from long layoff but has strong record on good going and remains lightly raced
runners_data.comment: Absent since November 2024 but on a competitive mark and one to watch in the betting
runners_data.spotlight: This is her first run since November 2024 and she needs to prove how much ability she retains; however, this lightly raced 6yo is on a competitive judged on her handicap form in autumn 2024 and it will be interesting to see how she goes in the betting on her return to action.

runners_data.name: Go Dante
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent Sandown record but below par recently, needs to rediscover December form
runners_data.comment: Below par since win in December but potential class act for yard with good record in this
runners_data.spotlight: Added to his excellent Sandown record when winning over 2m on soft in December; below par since, including a never-dangerous seventh when bidding for a third successive Imperial Cup back at Sandown, but this is the first time he's dropped to a Class 3 since winning at Cheltenham in December 2023; yard has won the last two runnings of this.

runners_data.name: King Jon Oliver
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won on stable debut, bounced back well from heavy ground flop at recent Uttoxeter run
runners_data.comment: The drop back down in trip could help and his trainer has a good record in this race
runners_data.spotlight: Won on stable debut at Fakenham (2m4f, good to soft) in January and bounced back from heavy-ground flop on handicap debut at Hereford when fourth at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good to soft) last month; shaped last time as though this shorter trip would help and trainer has a good record in this race.

races.paceDynamic: Skyjack Hijack and The Dog Thief will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to ensure a genuine gallop from the outset. King Jon Oliver may also track close behind from his prominent style, preventing any crawl. The strong pace will stretch the field and create opportunities for the large contingent of hold-up horses to finish strongly up the hill. This honest tempo strongly favours the hold-up performers who can produce their finishing kick late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders maintain a solid gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The strong pace will set up perfectly for the patient hold-up horses who can unleash their finishing speed in the final furlong. Flying Fortune, Serious Operator, and Go Dante are all proven late finishers who thrive off this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runners battle home
scenarios.trigger: If Skyjack Hijack bounces back to his winning form of late 2024
scenarios.body: The pace-setter could prove too strong for his rivals, particularly if The Dog Thief forces him into an honest gallop that suits his stamina. His six-race winning streak suggests he has the class when right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent runners strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes unsustainably fast between the two leaders
scenarios.body: Jack Hyde and King Jon Oliver can benefit from their handy positions as the front-runners weaken, allowing them to pick up the pieces. Their recent form suggests they're both capable of exploiting this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Returning performer shocks
scenarios.trigger: If Letterston Lily retains her ability after the long layoff
scenarios.body: Her excellent record on good going and light racing exposure could see her produce a surprise performance. The booking of Jack Tudor suggests connections are confident despite the absence.

watchPoints.text: Skyjack Hijack was pulled up on his return at Kelso and needs to prove his six-race winning streak form remains intact
Letterston Lily hasn't run since November 2024 and must demonstrate she retains her ability after the extended break
The early pace battle between Skyjack Hijack and The Dog Thief will determine whether the hold-up horses get their ideal setup
Nells Son has had wind surgery since his last disappointing hurdles effort and represents an unknown quantity
Flying Fortune runs just two days after his last outing, suggesting Mickey Bowen believes he's ready for a quick turnaround

races.name: One Place. Every Race. Racing TV Novices' Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Berkenshtaaap
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong recent RPR 102, benefits from traffic-heavy pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Only fair fourth on handicap debut but still early days for top yard which does well here
runners_data.spotlight: No immediate improvement for a switch to handicap company when fourth of nine over 2m5f at Haydock (good to soft) seven weeks ago but it's still early days for a good stable with a very strong Perth record.

runners_data.name: Valette
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from in-form Corbett yard, realistic handicap debut after Kelso winner Monday
runners_data.comment: Modest form in qualifying runs but more realistic chance now handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in three qualifying runs (trained in Ireland first two) but more realistic chance now handicapping for a yard which had a winner at Kelso on Monday.

runners_data.name: Mr Jukebox
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fresh off Exeter handicap win, extra 2f helps finishing kick, strong TS 96
runners_data.comment: Easy win on Exeter handicap debut last Friday; will take a bit of stopping in  same mood
runners_data.spotlight: Barely had to be nudged out to make a winning start to his handicap career at Exeter (2m2f, good) last Friday; the extra yardage here should help if anything and he'll take a bit of stopping under a 7lb penalty if showing up in a similar mood.

runners_data.name: Ayyadieh
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER
runners_data.comment: No improvement when 14.5fl third on handicap debut latest but it's still early days
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to improve on his maiden/novice form when 14.5l third of ten on Bangor handicap debut (2m3f, good) five weeks ago; still early days but he'll need to step up on that effort to go close here.

runners_data.name: The Coffey Boy
runners_data.note: Front runner who made all at Ayr C&D, only pace angle but from out-of-form Duncan yard
runners_data.comment: Made all over 2m4f at Ayr; only fifth over 2m there since but may fare better back at 2m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who made all and held on narrowly from Velvet Vulcan in conditional jockeys' race at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in February; not in the same form when fifth over 2m back at Ayr since but the return to 2m4f may see him in a better light.

runners_data.name: Zephlyn
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 445-day break, risky after such a long layoff

runners_data.name: Walk On Son
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with finishing fade tendency, wind surgery may help, 10lb claimer rides
runners_data.comment: Disappointing last twice but undergone wind surgery ahead of handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing in maiden hurdles on his last two outings but showed a bit of promise in similar races prior to that and has had wind surgery ahead of this handicap debut; also refitted with the tongue-tie he wore in bumpers.

runners_data.name: Pepite De Saphir
runners_data.note: Prominent runner switching yards after disappointing efforts, 3lb claimer takes over
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced but betting best guide now handicapping for new yard after absence
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdling debut fourth at Market Rasen in November 2024 but she failed to build on it in two subsequent runs for Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole; remains very lightly raced so she may still do better on her yard and handicap debut after 14 months off; also wears first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Velvet Vulcan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who ran well behind The Coffey Boy at Ayr, similar conditions today
runners_data.comment: Two near misses at Ayr this year (to The Coffey Boy latterly) but below par last twice
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Flat winner who showed best hurdles form when going very close at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in January/February, latterly to The Coffey Boy; does need to shrug off two lesser runs since, though.

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse improved at Carlisle but failed to back it up in handicaps since
runners_data.comment: Well treated on novice third in March but been able to confirm it in two handicaps since
runners_data.spotlight: Improved third in 2m1f Carlisle novice (soft) in February; well treated on that form but hasn't managed to reproduce it in two subsequent handicaps, although he probably pressed for home too far out when third back at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) in refitted cheekpieces (retained) three weeks ago; remains one who could click from a lowly mark.

runners_data.name: Seeyainthesuninn
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with modest form, well-held seventh last time out at Sedgefield
runners_data.comment: Has offered little in three runs this term, including back from break this month
runners_data.spotlight: Modest maiden hurdler; has offered little in his three runs this term, weakening into a well-held seventh back from a break at Sedgefield 23 days ago.

runners_data.name: Nae Bother At A'
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with fade tendency, 101 days off and drops back from 3m distance
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in two 3m handicaps seven months apart; off for a further 101 days
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on 3m course handicap debut last June (final start for Gary Rutherford) and fared little better for new yard at Ayr (3m again) seven months later; hopes are pinned on a shorter trip helping after a further 101 days off.

races.paceDynamic: The Coffey Boy will lead uncontested early, setting a sustainable gallop that suits his front-running style over this 2m4f trip. Five horses (Valette, Ayyadieh, Zephlyn, Pepite De Saphir, Nae Bother At A') want prominent positions, creating traffic congestion from 3 furlongs out as they jostle for tactical advantage. The hold-up brigade (Mr Jukebox, Berkenshtaaap, Walk On Son, Velvet Vulcan, King Kodiak, Seeyainthesuninn) will need clear runs in the final 2 furlongs. This race shape heavily favours patient hold-up horses who can weave through the prominent pack's inevitable traffic jam and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up heroes strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack creates the expected traffic jam from 3f out
scenarios.body: The congestion allows patient types with strong finishing kicks to pick their way through and sweep past tired leaders. Mr Jukebox and Berkenshtaaap have the class and tactical speed to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If The Coffey Boy gets uncontested fractions and the prominent pack fails to organize
scenarios.body: The leader's sustainable pace gives him enough in reserve to resist late challengers on this staying trip. His Ayr course-and-distance win proves he can handle this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent position pays
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners avoids the traffic and gets first run
scenarios.body: Smart positioning from the prominent pack allows someone like Valette or Zephlyn to strike before the hold-up horses get organized. Recent Kelso winner from Corbett's yard suggests stable form is strong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses early
scenarios.trigger: If The Coffey Boy goes too fast or falters early
scenarios.body: Without the controlling leader, the race becomes a messy affair where any running style can prevail depending on positioning luck. The most consistent recent performers benefit from the chaotic finish.

watchPoints.text: Traffic jam developing from 3f out as five prominent runners (Valette, Zephlyn, Pepite De Saphir, Nae Bother At A') converge on same tactical position
The Coffey Boy setting genuine fractions early - if he goes too fast he won't last home despite Ayr success
Mr Jukebox and Berkenshtaaap getting clear runs from the back as the main beneficiaries of expected pace collapse
Zephlyn returning from 445-day absence in prominent role - huge fitness question mark for Whillans runner
Walk On Son and King Kodiak both have finishing fade warnings but benefit if wind surgery works for former

races.name: One Place. Every Race. Racing TV Novices' Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Tyson

runners_data.comment: Non-runner

runners_data.comment: Losing run at 33 and remains to be seen if new headgear combination helps to snap it

runners_data.name: Karma De Cotte

runners_data.comment: Well beaten on last month's Carlisle handicap debut; tongue-tie worn then quickly removed
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 0-5 in Irish points and 0-4 under rules; took keen hold and weakened when fitted with a first-time tongue-tie on last month's Carlisle handicap debut; the tongue-tie is quickly removed.

runners_data.name: Gorvennec
runners_data.note: Prominent type who pulled up in handicap chase last time, questionable current form
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in hurdle and pulled up in chase this term; plenty to prove in new cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner; showed a bit in novice hurdles in November 2024 but tailed off in a novice hurdle and pulled up in a handicap chase in two outings this season over four months apart; fitted with first-time cheekpieces back hurdling; plenty to prove at present.

runners_data.name: Kap De Triomphe
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finally broke his duck at Plumpton over this trip last month
runners_data.comment: Won hurdle last month and fair fourth in chase ten days later; enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Irish bumper winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the ninth attempt in a handicap at Plumpton (2m4f, good to soft) last month; not far off that form when fourth on his Warwick chase debut (2m4f, good) ten days later; enters calculations back hurdling.

runners_data.name: De Deli Counter
runners_data.note: Front-runner who just won at Market Rasen, cheekpieces replace visor for uncomplicated type
runners_data.comment: Uncomplicated front-runner who gained a first win at Market Rasen 19 days ago; respected
runners_data.spotlight: A change of headgear (cheekpieces for visor) saw him land a first success at Market Rasen (2m4f, good) 19 days ago; this front-runner seems an uncomplicated type and should give it another good shot off 5lb higher.

runners_data.name: Humble Jumble
runners_data.note: Lead type who won Kelso bumper but hasn't reproduced bumper form over hurdles yet
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; fair third on two of four hurdle starts; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Kelso bumper in November 2024 (2m, good to soft); fair third in a novice hurdle there (2m6f, good to soft) on second jumps start; hasn't reproduced it in two subsequent outings but may fare better now switching to a handicap.

runners_data.name: Knockeranna Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse eased 2lb in weights, has reached frame in two of three 2m4f handicaps
runners_data.comment: Has reached frame in two of three handicaps and down another 2lb here
runners_data.spotlight: Has reached the frame in two of his three handicaps at around 2m4f this spring and being eased another 2lb can only help.

runners_data.name: Poet's Gale
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with unconvincing hurdles form but Sean Bowen booking suggests confidence
runners_data.comment: Unconvincing so far but Sean Bowen booked for Irish yard no stranger to Perth success
runners_data.spotlight: Not beaten far in a Galway bumper on debut; unconvincing hurdles form so far (including well held on completed start in handicaps) but Sean Bowen enlisted by an Irish yard no stranger to Perth success over the years, although not so much in recent times; betting interesting.

runners_data.name: Dublinofficecallin
runners_data.note: Front-runner beaten long way in three hurdle starts, needs major improvement
runners_data.comment: Well held in three qualifying runs but potential improver now handicapping up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten a long way in three qualifying runs over hurdles at up to 2m1f but did hint at promise on the first of two bumper starts and improvement wouldn't be a surprise now handicapping up in trip (bred for further).

runners_data.name: Defying Gravity
runners_data.comment: Ran pretty well when fifth of 13 on recent handicap debut; could be an each-way contender
runners_data.spotlight: Made his handicap debut at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) last month following wind surgery and a break and ran pretty well in fifth of 13, beaten 8l; races off the same mark today and could be an each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Roi Du Roume
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well third over course and distance two days ago

races.paceDynamic: Humble Jumble, De Deli Counter, and Dublinofficecallin will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with Humble Jumble likely to take them along having won his Kelso bumper and shown early pace. De Deli Counter just won as a front-runner at Market Rasen and will press the pace, while Dublinofficecallin adds further pressure up front. The sustained 2m4f tempo over good ground will test stamina reserves through the closing stages. This honest gallop strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay the trip and finish fastest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders go too fast and fade from the last hurdle
scenarios.body: The genuine pace will find out the front-runners' stamina limitations, allowing patient hold-up types to pick up the pieces. Horses with proven staying power who can quicken off a strong pace will dominate the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If De Deli Counter controls the tempo and kicks clear
scenarios.body: Having just won doing exactly this at Market Rasen, he could dictate terms and steal a decisive advantage. His uncomplicated front-running style suits this scenario perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grind
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders maintain a relentless gallop to the line
scenarios.body: The pace holds up throughout, creating a true test of stamina where only the most genuine stayers survive. This becomes a war of attrition favouring proven 2m4f+ performers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders go moderate and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Without genuine early pace, this turns into a tactical affair decided by who has the most speed from the last. Raw finishing pace becomes more important than stamina.

watchPoints.text: Humble Jumble could set unsustainable fractions if he leads from the start and gets competitive
De Deli Counter's front-running tactics worked last time but faces stronger pace pressure here
Star Vantage gets first-time visor after 33-race losing run, any market support significant
Karma De Cotte took keen hold with tongue-tie last time, needs to settle better
Tyson and Defying Gravity both non-runners reduce field size and change pace dynamics
